page: Microsoft Azure E16ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Eadsv7 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled with a local 945 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core score, and single-threaded gzip compression all placing in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics generally fall into the average tier, including stress-ng multi-core performance, Geekbench multi-core score, and large-block memory bandwidth. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression and text processing, alongside strong image processing. Large-model LLM inference (70B) is a notable bottleneck, registering in the bottom 25% for prompt processing, whereas small-model (135M) text generation reaches top-tier speeds.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E16ads_v7 offers a high-density memory allocation combined with fast local NVMe storage, making it a balanced choice for memory-intensive workloads without requiring a transition to specialized high-cost database hardware. The presence of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and a high clock speed ensures reliable performance for database operations, memory-cached applications, and text-processing pipelines. This server is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching layers, data decompression tasks, and small-scale language model inference.
